source.title: How Much Do Circuits Tell Us? Measuring the Consistency and Specificity of Language Model Circuits

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests IOI circuit properties in other models and evaluates circuit discovery and ablation choices. Its results qualify circuit claims by showing strong method dependence and a difference between component- and neuron-level circuits; it does not reproduce the original GPT-2 Small head circuit.
record.gate_note: IOI is one of six tasks, using the MIB dataset and S2-IO flip counterfactuals. The study does not test GPT-2 Small, identify the original 26 heads or 7 classes, or assess that circuit against the original faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria. It does not test backup-head takeover or IOI across varied prompt formats. Results cited from other work and results on unrelated tasks are not recorded here.
record.test_reason: IOI (MIB dataset, S2-IO flip) is one of six tasks. The study extracts IOI circuits in Gemma 2, Llama 3.2, Qwen3 and OLMo-2 checkpoints with EAP-IG and RelP. It reports their necessity, method agreement and cross-task overlap, and argues these circuit claims depend on granularity, method and metric. It never examines GPT-2 Small or the 26-head, 7-class circuit.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Component-level circuits are consistent and necessary but not task-specific; their overlap is driven by shared, mostly MLP, general-purpose components. Neuron-level and Gemma SAE-feature circuits are specific but inconsistent. Circuit claims depend on granularity and attribution method. Necessity tests alone do not justify claims of stable, unique task circuits.
record.recipe_differences: Uses automated EAP-IG and relevance patching to select consensus circuits in other models, then tests zero ablation against capacity-matched random controls and also evaluates mean ablation. It does not reconstruct the original GPT-2 Small head circuit or apply its full criteria.
record.method_sensitivity: Circuit structure depends on attribution method: EAP-IG and RelP have low same-task circuit overlap. Results also vary with circuit granularity: IOI component circuits have positive necessity while neuron-level IOI circuits leave accuracy unchanged. Across tasks, zero- and mean-ablation accuracy drops are highly correlated.

fits_no_version.finding: IOI circuit consistency across examples (Reuse@P) is high at component level and low at neuron level; Gemma SAE-feature reuse is 22%. IOI shows no specificity gap at any granularity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Automatically discovered IOI circuits are consistent across prompts and specific to IOI relative to other tasks.

record.problems: The study evaluates IOI in a single benchmark setup rather than comparing prompt variants. Its principal results do not use GPT-2 Small or identify the original head classes. Several IOI necessity outcomes are described qualitatively or in figures, and the mean-versus-zero ablation correlations are aggregated across tasks rather than reported for IOI alone. The paper notes limits in model scale and task complexity.
record.rows_left_out: No additional IOI-specific numerical results were stated in prose beyond those recorded. Figure-only model-level values were not transcribed where the flattened figure text did not reliably identify the value for each model.

untested.parts: Entirely: GPT-2 Small, the 26 heads, the 7 classes, and the faithfulness/completeness/minimality criteria.
Entirely: no name-mover ablation or backup-head analysis.
Whether other models have the same head classes and roles; whether the same circuit persists across checkpoints (OLMo tracks only reuse and necessity).
The original path-patching pipeline, ACDC and other methods; resample ablation; agreement with the 26-head circuit.
Faithfulness and completeness of the original circuit; prompt-distribution sensitivity; resample and other ablation types.
Entirely: a single IOI template setup, with no variation in name order, template or number of names.

missing.what: IOI-specific EAP-IG vs RelP circuit overlap per model: component 0.13, 0.16, 0.33, 0.29, 0.20; neuron 0.09, 0.08, 0.09, 0.08, 0.12.
Gemma-2-2B EAP-IG: IOI necessity near zero at component, neuron and feature granularity alike, contrary to the pooled positive component result.
IOI Jaccard overlap with each other task: EAP-IG component 0.47–0.61, RelP 0.29–0.34, neuron 0.01–0.03. Gemma EAP-IG Boolean and IOI circuits are identical (1.00).
Composition of IOI circuits: Gemma EAP-IG 5/95 heads/MLPs, Llama/Qwen 65–71% heads at K=10%. This contrasts with the attention-only original circuit.
OLMo-2-1B checkpoints: IOI K=30% circuit necessity is 50–70% through stage 1 but 9–13% after anneals. IOI Reuse@95 is 19–26%, falling to 7% after anneals.
Component task-specific set for IOI shows low necessity (selective ablation, P=100%).

record.verdict_notes: The original sources are not this study. IOI baseline accuracy is 100% in every model, so accuracy-based necessity is at ceiling; the log-prob contrast (r5) matters for this reason. The text contains an AI-review prompt quote in the AI use statement; it was ignored as data.

versions.untested_parts: The GPT-2 Small circuit, its 26 heads and 7 classes, their stated roles, and the original faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
Ablation of main name-mover heads and takeover by backup heads.

Whether other models reproduce the same head classes and roles as GPT-2 Small, and whether the cross-task overlap reflects reuse of those specific IOI computations rather than shared general-purpose components.
The original circuit-finding procedure itself and its equivalence to other ablation metrics beyond the study’s comparisons of EAP-IG with RelP and zero with mean ablation.
A direct evaluation of the original GPT-2 Small circuit’s faithfulness, completeness and minimality; prompt-distribution sensitivity beyond the study’s single IOI setup.
Comparisons across name orders, templates, and numbers of names.

rows.subject: Five main models; aggregate cross-task circuit results
rows.stage_stated: Gemma 2 2B Instruct and Llama-3.2-3B Instruct are instruct models; other stages not stated
rows.operation_detail: Measured Jaccard overlap between task circuits at K=10%, P=50%.

conditions.value: Addition, Boolean Logic, IOI, CopyColors MCQA, ARC Easy, ARC Challenge
Cross-task results summarized across models; task-pair-specific values shown in figures

rows.baseline: Not applicable; overlap is a measurement.
rows.value: Component circuits overlap heavily under EAP-IG and substantially under RelP; neuron-circuit overlap is near zero for nearly every task pair, except the two ARC tasks.
rows.note: IOI is among the task circuits compared. The authors caution that shared components may be general-purpose machinery rather than a shared task-specific algorithm.
rows.check: Component-level overlap is high but not task-specific: IOI overlaps unrelated Addition (0.47) about as much as similar CopyColors (0.53), and shared components are mostly MLPs. Neuron-level IOI overlap with other tasks is 0.01–0.03. 'Observed' overstates support for task reuse.

source_check.correct: For V3's preservation and reuse of identified IOI head classes and roles, state=cannot_determine. Cross-task component overlap is measured, but preserved IOI roles are not identified. General-purpose shared machinery is a preliminary interpretation, with the detailed case study restricted to Llama-3.2-3B.
source_check.problem: Generic component overlap does not establish incomplete preservation or reuse of the IOI head-class mechanism.

rows.subject: Five main models; aggregate IOI necessity result
rows.stage_stated: Gemma 2 2B Instruct and Llama-3.2-3B Instruct are instruct models; other stages not stated
rows.operation_detail: Zero-ablated the consensus task circuit and compared accuracy loss with a capacity-matched random control.

conditions.value: Qualitative report across the plotted model results

rows.measure: Necessity: accuracy-drop difference between task-circuit and capacity-matched control ablation
rows.baseline: Capacity-matched random ablation; exact IOI values not stated in prose
rows.value: Necessity is described as clearly positive for IOI at the component level.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals are shown in Figure 2; exact IOI interval values not stated in text.
rows.note: The paper states that positive necessity means the consensus circuit ablation hurts more than the capacity-matched control; it does not report an exact IOI value in the prose.
rows.check: This is the contrast arm for granularity dependence; the effect is clearly positive as aggregated. In Gemma-2-2B under EAP-IG, however, Appendix F.2 says IOI necessity is near zero at all three granularities, including component level. That model-level exception is not recorded.

rows.subject: Five main models; aggregate IOI necessity result
rows.stage_stated: Gemma 2 2B Instruct and Llama-3.2-3B Instruct are instruct models; other stages not stated
rows.operation_detail: Zero-ablated the consensus task circuit and compared accuracy loss with a capacity-matched random control.

conditions.value: Qualitative report across the plotted model results

rows.measure: Necessity: accuracy-drop difference between task-circuit and capacity-matched control ablation
rows.baseline: Capacity-matched random ablation; exact IOI values not stated in prose
rows.value: Necessity is described as low for IOI at the neuron level; the paper also states that ablating the IOI neuron-level circuit leaves IOI accuracy unchanged.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals are shown in Figure 2; exact IOI interval values not stated in text.
rows.note: The unchanged-accuracy statement is explicit; this contrasts with the positive component-level necessity result.
rows.check: Within V5 this row shows the dependence directly: the neuron-level IOI circuit leaves accuracy unchanged while the component circuit is necessary. IOI baseline accuracy is 100% in all models (Table 3), so accuracy is at ceiling.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Zero-ablated the 256 SAE latents shared across IOI examples at P=50%.
rows.baseline: not stated for the held-out evaluation set
rows.note: The paper interprets the shared latents as encoding the prompt template, while indirect-object selection varies across examples.
rows.check: Shows evaluation dependence: the consensus SAE-latent circuit (256 latents) leaves accuracy at 1.00. It is the comparison partner of r5, not an absent effect.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Ablated each example’s own top-10% SAE latents, rather than the consensus set.
rows.measure: Change in log-probability of the correct name
rows.value: The log-probability of the correct name decreases by 12 to 20 nats.
rows.note: This is a change in log-probability, not an accuracy decrease; the study contrasts it with the unchanged accuracy after ablating shared IOI latents.
rows.check: A 12–20 nat log-prob drop from per-example circuits, against unchanged accuracy for the consensus circuit. This shows the result depends on circuit selection and metric. 'Partial' is wrong for V5.

rows.subject: Five main models; aggregate same-task circuit comparisons
rows.stage_stated: Gemma 2 2B Instruct and Llama-3.2-3B Instruct are instruct models; other stages not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared circuits from EAP-IG and RelP on the same task.

conditions.value: Mean Jaccard overlap per model and task, summarized in text

rows.measure: Jaccard overlap between circuits found by the two attribution methods
rows.baseline: Not applicable; overlap is a measurement.
rows.value: Mean overlap is 0.23 at the component level and 0.16 at the neuron level.
rows.note: The paper also reports weak correlation between component scores from the two methods (mean Spearman ρ = 0.36).
rows.check: The values (0.23/0.16) are pooled over six tasks. IOI-specific values in Figure 13 are lower or similar and are not recorded: component overlap 0.13–0.33, neuron overlap 0.08–0.12.

rows.subject: Five main models; aggregate across model-task pairs
rows.stage_stated: Gemma 2 2B Instruct and Llama-3.2-3B Instruct are instruct models; other stages not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared accuracy drops under zero ablation and mean ablation of task circuits.

conditions.value: Correlation across task pairs; not IOI-specific

rows.measure: Correlation between accuracy drops under the two ablation types
rows.value: At P=50%, accuracy-drop correlations are r = 0.97 for component-level EAP-IG, r = 0.97 for component-level RelP, r = 0.86 for neuron-level EAP-IG, and r = 0.80 for neuron-level RelP.
rows.note: This aggregate comparison does not isolate IOI; the authors say their necessity and specificity findings hold under mean ablation.
rows.check: Not a V4 row: it compares ablation types for evaluating fixed circuits, not circuit recovery. For V5 it shows little ablation dependence between zero and mean ablation (r=0.97 component), so 'observed/supports' has the wrong direction. It is pooled over all tasks, not IOI-specific.

relationships.condition: IOI task circuits in Gemma 2, Llama 3.2 and Qwen3, K=10%, P=50%
relationships.reason: Component-level IOI circuits share many components with all tasks, related or not, and these are mostly general-purpose MLPs. Neuron-level IOI circuits barely overlap other tasks, so overlap does not show IOI-specific reuse (r1).
relationships.display_finding: At K=10% and P=50%, component circuits share mostly general-purpose MLPs across related and unrelated tasks, while neuron circuits barely overlap, leaving IOI-specific reuse unresolved.

relationships.condition: EAP-IG vs RelP in Gemma 2, Llama 3.2 and Qwen3, K=10%, P=50%
relationships.reason: The two methods' same-task circuits overlap only 0.23 (component) and 0.16 (neuron), with IOI-specific overlap of 0.13–0.33 (component). Score correlation is ρ=0.36 (r6; IOI values from Fig. 13).
relationships.display_finding: At K=10% and P=50%, same-task overlap was 0.23 for components and 0.16 for neurons, with score correlation ρ=0.36; IOI component overlap ranged from 0.13 to 0.33.

source_check.reason: Figure 13 gives IOI component overlaps of 0.13, 0.16, 0.33, 0.29 and 0.20 across the five models. This challenges agreement between these automated methods in this setting; r6's 0.23/0.16 overlaps and score correlation 0.36 pool tasks.

relationships.condition: IOI circuits, K=10%, P=50%, zero ablation
relationships.reason: IOI circuit necessity depends on unit granularity (component positive, neuron none) and on consensus vs per-example selection and metric. Accuracy stays at 1.00 while log-prob drops 12–20 nats (r2–r5).
relationships.display_finding: Necessity appeared at component granularity but disappeared at neuron granularity and varied with consensus versus per-example selection; accuracy remained 1.00 while log-probability fell 12–20 nats.

source_check.reason: r2–r3 establish aggregate granularity-dependent IOI necessity. In r4–r5, consensus SAE-latent ablation leaves accuracy at 1.00, whereas per-example selection lowers correct-name log probability by 12–20 nats; selection and metric change together.

relationships.condition: Zero vs mean ablation, pooled across six tasks including IOI
relationships.reason: Accuracy drops and necessity barely change between zero and mean ablation (r=0.97 component, 0.80–0.86 neuron, P=50%). Ablation dependence does not appear for this pair of choices; the result is not IOI-specific (r7).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy drops and necessity barely changed, with correlations of 0.97 for components and 0.80–0.86 for neurons at P=50% across six tasks including IOI.

relation.reason: Its own IOI circuit extraction and ablation results test method agreement and evaluation sensitivity.

tranche.reason: The study directly questions circuit interpretations using attribution-method disagreement, granularity-dependent necessity, and lack of task specificity.

source_check.notes: The aggregate positive component-level IOI necessity has a Gemma-2-2B EAP-IG exception: Appendix F.2 reports near-zero necessity at all three granularities. Table 3 baselines concern training examples; SAE top-K selection uses scored latents, not the entire dictionary.

statements.correction: Component-level task circuits overlap substantially; neuron-level overlap is near zero for most task pairs. In the Llama-3.2-3B EAP-IG shared core, 14 of 17 components are MLP blocks. General-purpose shared machinery: preliminary interpretation. Preserved IOI head classes and roles: not identified.
statements.problem: The overlap findings and evidential caution are correct, but preserved IOI head roles are untested rather than shown to have limited scope. General-purpose MLP function is hypothesized, not established across all three families.
